title: flywheel-teams: run the agent flywheel in repositories shared with other people
description:
Context: flywheel-teams lets a person run the agent flywheel (Claude Code and Codex swarms under ntm or frankenterm, with beads, Agent Mail and dcg) in repositories that other people also work in, without changing how the flywheel works for that person and without changing the repository for the other people. Three situations: a repository the operator does not own whose team has not adopted the flywheel (the operator overlay, M1); a repository the team owns where several people run the flywheel (team mode, M3); and the transitions between them. Principle (Ryan, 2026-10-24): once the overlay is installed and its config confirmed in a repository, running the flywheel there is just like running the flywheel anywhere.

Plan of record: docs/plans/2026-11-09-flywheel-teams.md (v1.1). AGENTS.md is the contract for working here: bash 3.2 plus jq only, shellcheck clean, every behaviour with a test and a planted negative under test/, no em dashes, nothing that names a client. This repository is public.

This is the root epic. Milestones: M0 bootstrap (2026-11-09), M1 the operator overlay accepted on the first client repository, M2 packaged for others, M3 team mode, M4 candidates (undecided). Section 9 of the plan is the work breakdown; each numbered item there is one bead under the milestone epics, and bead 28 (CI confirmed) sits here under M0.

Success per repository: fwt doctor --live green on both hosts before a swarm runs; a wave is pushed through the gate with no overlay or tooling file in any commit and no change to the team's instruction files; agents followed no extra steps compared with a normal flywheel repository. For team mode: two people run swarms in one repository for a week with no beads conflict left for a human that the rule could have resolved, and no lost claim.

Non-goals: forking or replacing ntm, br, bv, Agent Mail, dcg or ft; changing the solo flywheel; process for its own sake; a hosted service; any runtime beyond bash and jq.

title: Shared library lib/: placement detection, YAML-subset parser, legacy reader, generation, excludes, hook installation, recorded keys
description:
Context: flywheel-teams lets a person run the agent flywheel (Claude Code and Codex swarms under ntm or frankenterm, with beads, Agent Mail and dcg) in repositories that other people also work in, without changing how the flywheel works for that person and without changing the repository for the other people. Principle (Ryan, 2026-10-24): once the overlay is installed and its config confirmed in a repository, running the flywheel there is just like running the flywheel anywhere.

Plan of record: docs/plans/2026-11-09-flywheel-teams.md (v1.1). AGENTS.md is the contract for working here: bash 3.2 plus jq only, shellcheck clean, every behaviour with a test and a planted negative under test/, no em dashes, nothing that names a client. This repository is public.

Why: the guard, the CLI and the gate share the same primitives. One library means one behaviour and one set of tests. Plan sections 6.5, 6.6 and 6.7.

Build lib/ as bash files sourced by bin/fwt and hooks/agents-local-guard.sh (the guard must stay fast: source only what it needs). Bash 3.2 compatible; jq is the only parser.
- Repository root (git rev-parse --show-toplevel) and placement detection: overlay when AGENTS.local.md exists at the root; team when .flywheel/profile.yaml exists; legacy when a shell .flywheel/profile exists; none otherwise.
- Config parser for exactly the grammar in plan 6.6: key [a-z][a-z0-9_-]*; "key: value" split on the first ": "; values are a bare scalar, a single-quoted scalar, true, false, an integer, [], a flow list [a, b] of bare scalars, or a block list of "  - item" lines; a "#" preceded by a space starts a comment; no multi-line scalars, nesting, anchors or duplicate keys. Unknown keys, duplicates and anything else fail with the file and line number. Frontmatter is delimited by --- lines at the top of AGENTS.local.md; .flywheel/profile.yaml is the whole file. Output is a flat set of shell variables, or JSON with --json. Never sources a file. A prepush_checks entry splits on the first " => ". The version key is flywheel-teams; the pre-release spelling agents-local is accepted with a warning for doctor and rewritten by sync.
- Legacy shell profile reader: parses known FLYWHEEL_* keys against their allowed values, warns on invalid values, never sources (the same stance as the retired flywheel-profile.sh). Mapping per plan Appendix A.
- Placeholder filling for the templates ({{NAME}} tokens from the derived values in plan 6.7), canary generation (canary- plus eight hex digits from od -An -N4 -tx1 /dev/urandom), and detection of leftover tokens or <!-- fwt: --> markers.
- Generation of CLAUDE.local.md and the Codex file (AGENTS.md or AGENTS.override.md) from the team's file plus AGENTS.local.md without its frontmatter, canary last. First line: <!-- fwt <version> generated; do not edit. sources: <team file> <git hash-object>, AGENTS.local.md <git hash-object>. Doctrine changes go in AGENTS.local.md. -->. git hash-object, not sha256sum, which macOS lacks. Atomic write via a temporary file and mv.
- Exclude management for .git/info/exclude: lines between "# >>> fwt >>>" and "# <<< fwt <<<"; add missing lines, remove only our block, print what changed.
- Git hook installation (plan 6.5): when core.hooksPath is unset and .git/hooks/<name> is absent, write .git/hooks/<name>; otherwise write .git/fwt-hooks/<name>, a wrapper that runs our check on a copy of stdin and then execs the repository's own hook of the same name (from the previous hooksPath or .git/hooks) with that stdin, set core.hooksPath to .git/fwt-hooks, and record the previous value under fwt.teamHooksPath. Each installed hook carries a header with the fwt version so doctor can recognise it.
- Recorded keys in .git/config: fwt.seed, fwt.trunk, fwt.generated, fwt.teamHooksPath.
- Version stamps: fwt --version in every generated header and installed hook.
- State directory: ${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/flywheel-teams/<repo-hash>/ for logs, mode 0700, files 0600.

Tests (test/lib.test.sh): the parser accepts the documented grammar and rejects nested maps, anchors, multi-line strings and duplicate keys with the right line number; legacy mapping; generation reproduces a golden output for the four repository shapes (CLAUDE.md only, AGENTS.md only, both, neither); exclude add and remove are idempotent; hook installation in a plain repository and in one with core.hooksPath set, with the wrapper re-feeding stdin to a recording stub. Negative control: a mutant parser that sources the file must be caught by a fixture containing a shell command.

Depends on the spike for payload shapes and hook behaviour.

description:

Why: flywheel skills tell conductors to encode doctrine into AGENTS.md and to run br agents --add. In a normal repository that is right. In an overlay it would put the doctrine in front of the team's own agents. This is the one behaviour the overlay has to redirect. Plan section 6.2 and decision D12: the guard handles only what dcg cannot see (file edits through the hosts' tools and the refresh); the Bash rules are the dcg pack local.agents_local_guard (bead 5).

The hook runs on PreToolUse for both hosts and is inert unless AGENTS.local.md exists at the repository root (exit 0, no output, fast path first).
- Root: git -C "$(jq -r .cwd)" rev-parse --show-toplevel; file paths resolve against cwd.
- Deny edits through Claude Edit, Write, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit (file_path or notebook_path) and Codex apply_patch (Add, Update, Delete and Move paths parsed from tool_input.command) to any AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.override.md at any depth that git ls-files --error-unmatch reports tracked, and to the two generated files at the root. Reason text: "This repository's flywheel doctrine lives in AGENTS.local.md; the team's instruction files are theirs, and the generated files are rebuilt from it." Edits to AGENTS.local.md itself are allowed.
- Refresh: if the generated Codex file's recorded hashes differ from the current team file and AGENTS.local.md, run fwt sync --quiet --no-seed when fwt resolves on PATH, then allow; otherwise allow and leave the file for doctor.
- Fail open with no output when jq is absent, the payload is not JSON, or cwd is not inside a repository; doctor reports the first two.
- Matchers: Claude Edit|Write|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit; Codex ^apply_patch$.
- Output on deny: {"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"deny","permissionDecisionReason":"..."}}. Nothing else on stdout, ever. Read all of stdin. Shebang #!/bin/bash and bash 3.2 compatible, because it is copied into ~/.claude and ~/.codex and runs without Homebrew.

Tests (test/guard.test.sh): both hosts' payloads for each rule from test/fixtures/; an inert repository; AGENTS.local.md edits allowed; a nested tracked CLAUDE.md denied; stale-file refresh with a stub fwt on PATH and without; malformed JSON and missing jq fail open; a 1 MB stdin. Negative control under test/mutants/: a guard allowing CLAUDE.md edits must be caught.

install.sh [--check | --dry-run | --uninstall] [--agent claude|codex|all]:
1. Links bin/fwt into ~/.local/bin (or $FWT_BIN_DIR), replacing only a link that points into this checkout.
2. Copies hooks/agents-local-guard.sh into each host's home and merges one PreToolUse group per host into ~/.claude/settings.json and ~/.codex/hooks.json. Matchers: Claude Edit|Write|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit; Codex ^apply_patch$ (one regex group, one trust entry). Keep the guarantees of the existing agent-hooks installer in Ryan's skills repository (tools/agent-hooks/install.sh): find our group by command path and replace in place or append at the end, never reorder (Codex trust keys are positional); refuse malformed, symlinked or shared configs; timestamped .bak copies and atomic writes; idempotent; --check exits 1 on drift; --dry-run reports without writing; --uninstall removes only ours.
3. Copies packs/*.yaml into ~/.config/dcg/packs/ without touching ~/.config/dcg/config.toml. Prints the config line to add if the operator wants a pack enabled globally; the overlay enables packs per repository through .dcg.toml.
4. Sets project_doc_max_bytes = 131072 in ~/.codex/config.toml: inserts the line before the first "[" line with awk, after a timestamped backup, only when the key is absent or lower; leaves a symlinked config.toml alone and prints the line to add; --check returns 1 until the key is present.

Why: an outcome check at the point where work leaves the machine, using git's normal pre-push hook, the same pattern as Ryan's template. Agents push through it as normal, and the no-bypass pack stops them skipping it. Plan section 6.5.

The hook reads git's stdin (local ref, local sha, remote ref, remote sha), runs git fetch --quiet origin first (and warns when offline that the range may include upstream commits), and checks each pushed range: <remote sha>..<local sha>, or <local sha> --not --remotes for a new branch.

Always:
1. No overlay file or tooling folder in the commits (the exclude list is the source).
2. No change to the team's instruction files (a tracked AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.override.md).
3. No push to protect_branches (default: the default branch when a trunk is set).

From the configuration:
4. protect_existing: no modify, rename or delete of a matching path that exists at the merge base with origin/<default>. An agent's own new files stay editable (the append-only migrations case).
5. prepush_checks: each must exit 0. An entry "<glob> => <cmd>" runs only when the pushed commits touch matching paths. With prepush_checks_in: archive (default) the checks run in a git archive <sha> extraction under $TMPDIR, so other agents' uncommitted edits are not what is tested; with prepush_checks_in: worktree they run in the working tree, and the gate refuses while git status --porcelain lists modified tracked files.

On failure: print the commit, the file and the check, and exit 1. Print timings per check. The hook carries the fwt version in its header.

Tests (test/gate.test.sh): real commits against a local bare remote, one fixture per check, a clean pass, a path-conditioned check that does and does not run, a new-branch push, both prepush_checks_in modes, the offline warning (origin unreachable).
